tagline: Design CSS box-shadow with live preview and copy the code instantly
pageDescription: Create the perfect CSS box-shadow with this free online generator. Drag sliders for horizontal and vertical offset, blur, spread, color and opacity, toggle inset shadows, and stack multiple shadow layers — all with a real-time live preview. Whether you need a soft drop shadow for cards and buttons or a layered, neumorphic effect, just tweak the controls until it looks right, then copy and paste the ready-to-use box-shadow code into your stylesheet. No signup, works in your browser, and includes handy presets to start from.

instructions.title: How to use the CSS Box Shadow Generator

steps.title: Start from a preset (optional)
steps.description: Click a preset like Subtle, Medium or Layered to load a starting shadow, then fine-tune it.

steps.title: Adjust the sliders
steps.description: Drag Offset X/Y to move the shadow, Blur to soften it, and Spread to grow or shrink it. The preview updates live.

steps.title: Pick color and opacity
steps.description: Choose a shadow color and set its opacity. Toggle Inset to render the shadow inside the box.

steps.title: Add more layers
steps.description: Click Add layer to stack multiple shadows for depth — each layer has its own controls.

steps.title: Copy the CSS
steps.description: Click Copy CSS to grab the full box-shadow declaration and paste it into your stylesheet.

proTips: Stack two layers — a tight dark one and a wide soft one — for realistic depth
Use a negative spread to keep the shadow tighter than the box
Lower opacity (10–25%) usually looks more natural than solid black
Inset shadows are great for pressed buttons and input fields
Offset 0/0 with blur creates an even glow around the element
Copy the code straight into a Tailwind arbitrary value: shadow-[…]
troubleshooting: No shadow visible: increase blur or opacity, or check offsets aren't 0 with 0 blur
Shadow clipped: a parent with overflow:hidden can cut off the shadow
Inset not showing: inset shadows render inside the element, not around it
Color looks off: opacity multiplies the picked color — raise it for a stronger shadow
Too harsh: reduce opacity and increase blur for a softer look
